content.title: About
content.content: Cooked seaweed with added fat is a marine plant that has been blanched and then lightly fried in a small amount of vegetable oil. It has a tender texture, a mildly salty sea flavor, and a subtle aroma. The product is commonly used in Asian cuisine as a side dish, salad ingredient, soup garnish, or sushi wrap.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Seaweeds are among the oldest living organisms on Earth, existing for over 600 million years.
More than 10,000 seaweed species are known, but edible varieties most often include kelp, nori and wakame.
Frying in oil enhances the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins such as vitamin D and carotenoids.
Seaweeds are a rich natural source of iodine, essential for thyroid hormone production.
In Japan, cooked seaweed is traditionally served with soy sauce and vinegar as a snack called “okonomiyaki”.

items.title: High in iodine
items.content: Iodine supports the synthesis of thyroid hormones that regulate metabolism.

items.title: Source of polysaccharides
items.content: Polysaccharides like alginates help maintain a healthy gut microbiota.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Seaweed provides vitamin E, carotenoids and polyphenols that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: The polyunsaturated fats from the added oil may help lower LDL cholesterol levels.

items.title: Rich in minerals
items.content: Calcium, magnesium, iron and potassium in seaweed are important for bones, muscles and nerve function.

items.title: Excess iodine
items.content: Consuming too much iodine can disrupt thyroid function, especially in susceptible individuals.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Cooked seaweed is often salted; people monitoring sodium intake should limit portions.

items.title: Seafood allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to marine algae.

items.title: Contaminants
items.content: Seaweed can accumulate heavy metals and toxins from the ocean; choose products from reputable sources.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cooked seaweed with fat can be enjoyed as a snack, added to salads, soups, rice or noodle dishes, and used as a wrapper for sushi rolls. It is easy to slice into strips or pieces. Serve with a drizzle of soy sauce or a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the product in a sealed container in the refrigerator at 0 °C–4 °C. It usually stays fresh for 7–10 days. Discard if it develops an off‑odor, discoloration, or visible mold.
